title: Pressure balance relation
description: Essential: Student must state that the internal pressure exceeds atmospheric pressure by 4γ/R₀ due to surface tension.

title: Ideal gas law application
description: Important: Student correctly applies the ideal gas law to relate ρT to pressure for both internal and external air.

title: Final ratio expression
description: Essential: Student derives and presents the final answer for part (1) as (ρᵢTᵢ)/(ρₐTₐ) = 1 + 4γ/(R₀Pₐ).

title: Numerical substitution accuracy
description: Important: Student correctly substitutes given numerical values into derived expressions for parts (2), (3), and (5).

title: Buoyancy and weight analysis
description: Important: Student correctly calculates total weight (soap film + internal air) and buoyant force for the flotation condition.

title: Force balance with drag
description: Important: Student sets Stokes' drag force equal to net downward force (weight minus buoyancy) for parts (4) and (5).

title: Electric pressure inclusion
description: Important: Student accounts for the electrostatic repulsion pressure (q²/(32π²ε₀R₁⁴)) in the pressure balance for the charged bubble.

title: Small-change approximation
description: Optional: Student correctly applies the binomial approximation (1+x)^n ≈ 1+nx to simplify the equation for ΔR in part (7).

title: Sign or unit error
description: Pitfall: Student makes a sign error in the pressure balance (e.g., Pᵢ = Pₐ - 4γ/R₀) or misplaces factors in the electrostatic pressure.

title: Neglecting soap film mass
description: Pitfall: Student omits the mass of the soap film (4πR₀²ρₛt) in the weight calculation for flotation and drag balance.
